codes.justification: The clause is part of the waiver-of-claims procedure, requiring the party who gave notice of a claim to submit a detailed account of the amount claimed within a reasonable time. This is a step in the notice and claim process for matters in question between the parties.

The clause allocates risk between Owner and Contractor through mutual indemnification for losses caused by negligence or failure to fulfil the Contract, and it limits indemnity to claims provided for in the Contract.
The clause governs set-off and deduction from amounts the terminating party is entitled to be paid under 8.4.4, which affects payment entitlements on termination.
It allocates responsibility for loss and damage arising from termination between the parties. Recovery is limited to the exceptions in the waiver of liability provision.
The clause allocates responsibility for damage not caused by the Contractor: the Contractor must make it good while the Owner bears the resulting price and time adjustment.
It expressly provides for adjustment of the Contract Price and Contract Time through the change provisions in GC 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 (Change Orders and Change Directives).
It requires the Contractor to perform repair work to make good damage to the Work and, if directed, to Owner's property.
The clause recognizes the Contract Documents as the contractual baseline, which may be amended only through the procedures the Contract Documents provide.
By restricting amendment of the Contract to the mechanisms in the Contract Documents, it points to formal change provisions such as Change Orders and Change Directives.

Sub-clause .1 requires the Owner to provide its requirements and actively participate in developing and documenting the Project Objectives, which are jointly developed during the Validation Phase before construction.
Sub-clause .2 requires the Owner to provide geotechnical and environmental impact reports relevant to the Work.
The clause gives the Owner audit access to records relating to the Cost of the Work, which is the administration mechanism of a cost-plus / GMP / Target Cost arrangement in CCDC 3.
Located in Part 5 Payment, the clause requires records to be preserved for a period tied to the final certificate for payment, so it relates to payment verification and certification.

The clause restricts amendment of the Contract to the mechanisms provided in the Contract Documents (e.g., Change Orders and Change Directives), addressing how the Contract and Work may be formally changed.
It treats the Contract as a fixed baseline that may only be modified through the formal change provisions of the Contract Documents.

The clause adjusts the Contract Time and provides cost reimbursement to the Contractor when a stop work order causes delay, which is an adjustment to Contract Time and Price outside the Contractor's fault.
It allocates the risk of delay from a stop work order not caused by the Contractor to the Owner through a time extension and reimbursement of costs.

The clause sets the Payment Certifier's 7-day duty to certify Substantial Performance, or give written reasons for not doing so. This certification is a payment-related step under Part 5 and drives holdback release and payment timing.

The clause allocates responsibility by allowing the Design-Builder to rely on the Owner's Advisor's written instructions, subject to notified limits, and by excluding any duty or responsibility of the Owner's Advisor to the Design-Builder, Consultants, Subcontractors and Suppliers.
Gives the Construction Manager total control of the Work and requires it to direct and supervise the Work, which sets a core duty on how the Work is organized, supervised and executed.
Makes the Construction Manager responsible for ensuring conformity with the Contract Documents, which allocates responsibility for conformity of the Work.

The clause addresses the Consultant's finding on a concealed or unknown conditions claim, which concerns whether an adjustment to Contract Price or Contract Time is justified, and requires written notice of that finding.

The Consultant's written finding that no change is justified is the step that can trigger a matter in question or dispute process under the Contract, but the clause does not itself establish dispute resolution.

The clause reserves the Owner's right to award separate contracts and use its own forces on other parts of the Project, which shapes how and by whom the Project is performed alongside the Contractor's Work.

The Consultant receives and reviews written warranties and related documents provided by the Contractor, a verification step that relates to compliance with the Contract, though it is not tied to fabricated Products before incorporation.

The clause requires adjustment of the Contractor's Fee, GMP, Target Contract Price and Contract Time through the change provisions (GC 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, Change Order and Change Directive) for repair of damage not caused by the Contractor.
It allocates responsibility for damage the Contractor is not responsible for: the Contractor makes it good, and the Owner bears the resulting cost and time adjustment.
It expressly provides for adjustment of the GMP, Target Contract Price and Contractor's Fee, which administers the target-cost mechanism.
The clause sets the content required in a Notice in Writing to preserve a claim that would otherwise be waived, which allocates the risk of losing a claim if the notice is deficient.
It governs the form of claims, including the intention to claim, the nature and grounds, and the estimated quantum, and this is part of the claims process under the Contract.

Requires the Contractor to deliver a comprehensive list of items to be completed or corrected, and preserves responsibility to complete or correct omitted items, addressing identification and correction of deficient Work.
Sets a Contractor duty in the process of concluding the Work (applying for Ready-for-Takeover) and confirms continuing responsibility to complete the Contract despite omissions from the list.
States that failure to list an item does not alter the Contractor's responsibility to complete the Contract, allocating responsibility for incomplete or non-conforming Work to the Contractor.
The clause requires the Contractor to proceed promptly with a change in the Work upon receipt of a Change Directive, which is a formal change mechanism.
It imposes a duty on the Contractor on how to perform the Work, namely to proceed promptly with the directed change.
The clause sets the content a Notice in Writing must have to preserve a claim that would otherwise be waived. This allocates the risk of losing claim rights between the parties.
The clause governs the form and content of claim notices, requiring the nature, grounds and estimated quantum of the claim, which supports claims for adjustment under the Contract.
The clause obliges the Design-Builder to provide the Design Services, which establishes design responsibility that underlies the Construction Documents and the Work.

The clause fixes the Contract as a baseline that may be modified only through the amendment procedures set out in the Contract Documents, which is the restriction on changes that Design Lock-In describes.
By limiting amendments to those provided for in the Contract Documents, the clause points to the formal change mechanisms (Change Orders and Change Directives) for adjusting the Contract.
The clause addresses disposal, storage and rendering harmless of toxic or hazardous substances at the Place of the Project in accordance with legislation, which is an environmental obligation.
It allocates responsibility to the Owner for pre-existing toxic or hazardous substances present before the Trade Contractor commenced the Work, which assigns contractual risk.
Establishes the Contractor's broad duty to provide and pay for labour, Products, equipment and services necessary for performing the Work in accordance with the Contract.
Allocates to the Contractor responsibility and cost for supplying all resources needed for the Work, which is an implied allocation of performance risk.

The clause governs how the Design-Builder organizes performance of the Work by selecting Subcontractors, Suppliers and Other Consultants, and gives the Owner a right to object to a proposed one for reasonable cause.
The Owner's right to object to a proposed party for reasonable cause before the subcontract is signed acts as a mitigation control over who performs the Work, allocating a selection-related risk.

The clause sets the Owner's obligation and timing (28 calendar days after receipt of an application) for paying the Construction Manager for Pre-construction Services, and requires compliance with Payment Legislation.
The clause expressly addresses toxic and hazardous substances at the Place of the Work and the Owner's duty to limit exposure and property damage from them.
It allocates to the Owner responsibility to take reasonable steps to manage the risk from pre-existing hazardous substances, including exposure and property damage.

PITs (Consultant, Contractor, other parties) participate in the Target Value Design process, evaluating constructability and Added Value Incentive Items and optimizing design, which involves contractor participation in developing design before or alongside construction.

Clause requires PITs to optimize and coordinate the design in accordance with the Base Program and collaborate on selection and installation of materials and systems, addressing design coordination and compatibility with the Work.
The clause concerns toxic or hazardous substances at the Place of the Work and the investigation of their existence and significance, which is an expressly environmental matter.

It sets a procedure for when the parties disagree: an independent qualified expert retained by the Owner investigates and reports to both parties, which works as a mechanism for resolving a matter in question.
The expert determines whether the Contractor brought the substances onto the site, which fixes responsibility for the hazardous substances, and the Owner bears the cost of the investigation.
The clause fixes the Contract as the baseline that may be amended only through the procedures in the Contract Documents, so changes must follow formal change provisions.
It governs how the Contract can be amended, which implies the formal change mechanisms (Change Orders, Change Directives) as the sole route to adjusting the Work, price or time.
Allows either party to submit a claim for adjustment of the Contract Price when post-bid changes in laws or codes affect the cost of the Work, following the GC 6.6 claims procedure.
Allocates the risk of post-bid changes in applicable laws and regulations by providing a claim mechanism for the resulting cost impact.

The clause allocates the risk of taxes and customs duties in effect at the Change Order date to the Construction Manager by including them in the Contract Price, and it carves out Value Added Taxes, which the Owner pays.

The clause requires the Owner and Contractor to agree adjustments to the Contractor's Fee, GMP, Target Contract Price and Contract Time when a proposed Subcontractor or Supplier changes, which is a change-driven adjustment of price and time.
It expressly provides for adjustment of the GMP, Target Contract Price and Contractor's Fee, which are administered under the cost-plus/target cost mechanism.
The clause sets a duty on the Construction Manager governing how the Work is performed and supervised: maintaining order and discipline among employees and using only skilled workers.
The clause governs how completion prerequisites for the Work are handled when deferred, so it sets a broader duty on completing the Work and reaching Ready-for-Takeover.
It allocates the consequence of deferral, in that conditions beyond the Contractor's control or agreed deferral do not delay Ready-for-Takeover, which protects the Contractor from delay.

Makes the Contractor responsible for construction means, methods, techniques and procedures and for coordinating the parts of the Work, which is a core duty governing how the Work is performed and organized.
Expressly assigns responsibility for construction 'sequences' and coordination of the various parts of the Work, addressing the order in which portions proceed.
Allocates responsibility for means, methods and sequencing to the Contractor rather than the Owner or Consultant, implicitly placing the associated risk on the Contractor.
The clause deals with mould, an environmental hazard, and requires the Owner to remediate or dispose of it safely.
It assigns the Owner responsibility for mould not caused by the Contractor. The Owner bears the remediation cost, delay costs and indemnity, which reallocates risk.
It provides for reimbursement of the Contractor's costs and an extension of Contract Time, which adjust the Contract Price and Contract Time.

The clause requires contingency allowance expenditures to be authorized and valued through the Owner's right to make changes, Change Orders and Change Directives, which is the formal change mechanism adjusting the Work and Contract Price.

The clause allocates responsibility between Owner and Construction Manager for obtaining and paying for approvals, permits and easements, which is an allocation of contractual responsibility and associated risk.

The clause governs how the Work proceeds when the Owner occupies part or all of it before Ready-for-Takeover, conditioning that occupancy on the Trade Contractor's agreement, which affects the organization of performance.

Requiring the affected Trade Contractor's agreement to early occupancy, which cannot be unreasonably withheld, balances and manages the parties' exposure and responsibility arising from early occupancy.
The clause allocates responsibility between Owner and Contractor for obtaining and paying for approvals, permits, and easements, with exceptions for those assigned to the Contractor.

The clause requires the PMT to set a reasonable date for finishing the Work after Ready-for-Takeover of a part or the whole of the Work. This addresses the timing and order in which portions of the Work are completed.
The clause sets a duty on the PMT to organize and fix the finishing of the Work following Ready-for-Takeover. This governs how the Work is brought to completion.
Addresses responsibility for compliance of the Contract Documents with laws and codes, and the Contractor's duty to report variances between the documents and regulations to the Consultant.
Allocates risk by relieving the Contractor of responsibility for verifying that the Contract Documents comply with laws, and by setting a duty to notify on variance.
Requires the Consultant to issue required changes to the Contract Documents through GC 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 (Change Orders and Change Directives) when variances or changes in law arise.

The clause fixes the Contract as the baseline that may be amended only through the procedures in the Contract Documents, which recognizes a formal baseline that is changed only by the contract's change provisions.
By restricting amendments of the Contract to the mechanisms in the Contract Documents, such as Change Orders, it governs how the Work and Contract Price may be formally adjusted.
The clause gives the Contractor total control of the Work and requires it to direct and supervise the Work, which is a core duty governing how the Work is performed and supervised.
By placing control and supervision with the Contractor to ensure conformity with the Contract Documents, the clause assigns responsibility for conformity of the Work to the Contractor.
Sets interest on late payments due under the Contract or an award, addressing payment timing and consequences of non-payment.
Paragraph 5.2.2 applies interest to settlement amounts of claims in dispute resolved under Part 8 Dispute Resolution or otherwise, and to amounts awarded by adjudication, arbitration or court.
The clause sets out the Change Order process: the Consultant describes a proposed change and the Construction Manager presents an adjustment to the Fee and the Contract Time.
The clause allocates responsibility for extended warranties: the Construction Manager is limited to obtaining them, and the warrantor solely bears the obligations under them.

Requires information and documentation prepared or received before termination during Validation to be returned to the party who prepared it or destroyed, which addresses rights in and control over Contract-related documents and implies they remain with their preparers.

The clause sits in Part 8 Dispute Resolution and preserves parties' rights and recourses provided they give the Notice in Writing required under the dispute process and follow the Consultant's instructions, tying it to the matters-in-question procedure.
The clause sets payment timing (28 calendar days from invoice) for Services properly performed up to the effective termination date, including reimbursable expenses and taxes.

The clause sets out how and when applications for payment on account of the Fee for Construction Services and the Cost of the Work are submitted monthly to the Owner and Consultant as the Work progresses.

The clause continues the parties' obligations for quality, correction and warranty of Work performed up to termination, which preserves the duty to correct defective or non-conforming Work after the Contract ends.
By keeping quality, correction and warranty obligations in force after termination, the clause allocates continuing responsibility for the conformity of Work already performed.
The clause begins the payment certification process, addressing receipt by the Consultant and Owner of the Contractor's application for payment under GC 5.3 PAYMENT.
Sub-clause .1 gives the Construction Manager and Consultant authority to require inspection or testing of work whether fabricated, installed or completed.
Sub-clause .1 gives authority to reject work that does not conform to the Contract Documents, which is the identification and rejection of non-conforming Work.
Sub-clause .3 requires the Construction Manager and Consultant to prepare Change Orders and Change Directives under GC 6.2 and 6.3.

The clause sets out the administrative roles and authority of the Construction Manager and Consultant over the Work, including rejection, interpretations and findings on the Work, which govern how the Work is supervised under the Contract Documents.

The clause states that the authority to act, or a decision not to act, creates no duty or responsibility of the Construction Manager or Consultant to the Trade Contractor or others, which allocates responsibility and limits liability.
Sub-clause .2 provides for written interpretations and findings within 5 Working Days without partiality, which is the first step in the matters-in-question process.
The clause requires the Owner to give prompt written notice of observed defects and deficiencies during the warranty period, which triggers the correction of defective Work.
It allocates to the Owner a duty to notify promptly, which conditions the Design-Builder's responsibility for warranty correction of non-conforming Work.

The clause sets a requirement for each application for progress payment after the first: a statutory declaration (CCDC 9A) on how previously received payments were distributed. This is a payment application and certification mechanic.
The clause makes payments subject to the applicable lien legislation where required, which addresses payment provisions and compliance with legislation governing payment.
Defines the reimbursable Cost of the Work, which is the cost-plus basis on which the fee and any GMP are administered.
Items .13 and .14 make insurance premiums reimbursable and cover losses within deductibles or above collectible amounts under the GC 11.1 policies.
Item .2 makes the cost of transporting Products reimbursable, and item .1(3) covers personnel expediting the production or transportation of materials.
Item .10 makes the cost of quality assurance, such as independent inspection and testing services, a reimbursable cost.
The clause allocates contractual risk by mutually waiving claims among the parties, subject to enumerated exceptions such as willful misconduct, third-party claims and latent substantial defects.
Exception .6 preserves claims for which indemnification under the specified insurance policies is or would have been available, tying the waiver to the insurance requirements in GC 9.1.
Exception .2 expressly refers to violations of applicable environmental legislation as a claim not waived.

Exception .8 preserves claims for substantial defects or deficiencies in the Design Services or the Work not discoverable before the end of the Warranty Phase, and exception .3 preserves warranty claims.
Exception .4 preserves claims for payment of amounts due under the Contract from the waiver.

Imposes a duty on the Trade Contractor to locate underground utilities and structures, in collaboration with the Construction Manager, before commencing any work. This governs how the Work is organized and carried out.
Requires the Trade Contractor to identify underground hazards before starting work, which assigns responsibility for and mitigates the risk of damage to utilities and structures.

Under the Changes in the Work part, the clause conditions any request for extension of Contract Time on a 10 Working Day demand period when the Consultant fails to furnish instructions, which governs adjustment of Contract Time claims.
The clause turns on whether a schedule for furnishing instructions exists under GC 2.2.13 and sets a timing threshold (10 Working Days) for time extension requests.
The clause allocates and transfers liability risk between the parties through mutual indemnification for specified claims. It also waives indemnity for all other claims.

The clause grants the Owner, through the Construction Manager, the right to make additions, deletions or revisions to the Work by Change Order or Change Directive, and to change the Contract Time by Change Order.

The clause identifies and lists the documents that make up the Contract Documents (agreement, definitions, general conditions, specifications, drawings, addenda). This fixes the contractual baseline against which later changes are measured, although the clause does not itself mention change procedures.

Makes the Contractor solely responsible for construction means, methods, techniques and procedures and for coordinating the parts of the Work, which is a broad duty governing how the Work is performed and organized.
Expressly places responsibility for construction sequences and coordination of the various parts of the Work on the Contractor, which addresses the order in which portions of the Work proceed.
The 'solely responsible' wording allocates responsibility for means, methods and coordination to the Contractor, assigning the associated risk.
The clause governs the final payment application process, including the Consultant's timed review and advice on the validity of the application, which is payment certification mechanics.
The Consultant must 'review the Work' to verify the application's validity, implying an on-site review of the Work by an authorized party.
Requires the Contractor to provide, maintain and pay for Contract security (e.g., bonds), which transfers and mitigates the Owner's risk of Contractor non-performance.

The clause governs handling of the statutory holdback amount, requiring the Owner to deposit it in a joint bank account before the lien-legislation holdback period expires, which is a holdback and payment legislation compliance matter.
The clause fixes the one-year warranty period from Substantial Performance, which sets the period during which the Design-Builder is responsible for conformity of the Work.
Requires the Design-Builder to submit Shop Drawings to authorities having jurisdiction for approval, which is a form of review by authorities as required for the Work.
Shop Drawings illustrate details of fabricated Products; requiring authority approval acts as a verification of compliance before fabrication and incorporation into the Work.
The Owner's review does not relieve the Design-Builder of responsibility for errors, omissions or meeting Contract Document requirements, which allocates conformity risk to the Design-Builder.
Addresses the Owner's review of Shop Drawings for conformity to the intent of the Contract Documents, a verification step before fabrication and incorporation into the Work.
Concerns consistency of Shop Drawings with the Contract Documents and responsibility for errors or omissions in them.
Deviations from the Contract Documents are accepted only expressly by Change Order.
The clause makes the Trade Contractor responsible for the proper performance of the Work, which is a general duty governing how the Work is performed.
It allocates responsibility for performance to the Trade Contractor and limits it to what the design and Contract Documents permit, so the risk of design inadequacy stays with the Owner.

The Trade Contractor's responsibility is tied to the extent the design and Contract Documents permit proper performance. This addresses the interface between design adequacy and performance of the Work.
Sets a duty governing how the Work is performed by requiring Products to be new and of consistent quality, subject to the Consultant's acceptance.
Requires unspecified Products to be of consistent quality and acceptable to the Consultant before use, which is a compliance and verification check before incorporation into the Work.

The clause adjusts the Profit Pool by formula based on the difference between the Final Target Cost and the Base Target Cost as determined by the PMT, which administers the target-cost and fee mechanism.
It relies on the validated Base Target Cost as the baseline and on the Final Target Cost confirmed at the end of the Design/Procurement Phase, and measures adjustments against that baseline.
The clause sets the Contractor's basic duty to perform the Work required by the Contract Documents at the Place of the Work, which is a broad Work-execution obligation.
The clause preserves the Owner's obligation to pay the Fee for Services and reimbursable expenses in accordance with the Contract, so the liability limitation does not affect payment obligations.
The clause carves the Owner's payment obligation out of the limitation of liability, which sets how liability is allocated between the parties.

The clause allocates the consequence of an uncorrected default to the defaulting team member: the SMT may terminate its participation and keeps its other rights and remedies. This is a contractual risk-allocation and remedy mechanism.

The clause requires the Contractor to submit a schedule of values before the first application for payment so that payment applications can be evaluated, which is a payment application and certification mechanic.
The clause sets the dating and payment period for applications for progress payment, which is a core payment-application mechanic.

The clause requires the Construction Manager to notify the Consultant when work is ready for tests, inspections or approvals and to arrange inspections by other authorities, which establishes inspection procedures and access.
It sets a duty on the Construction Manager governing how the Work is organized and performed, by requiring it to arrange and notify inspections as part of executing the Work.

The clause sets out a formal dispute-resolution step: after 10 Working Days from the responding party's Notice in Writing, the parties must request the Project Mediator to help resolve unresolved disputes under CCDC 40 mediation rules.

The clause assigns the Consultant the task of preparing Change Orders and Change Directives under GC 6.2 and 6.3, which are the formal mechanisms for adjusting the Work, Contract Price and Contract Time.

The Consultant reviews and acts on Shop Drawings, samples and other submittals, which verifies compliance of Products and fabricated items with the Construction Documents before they are incorporated into the Work.
Review of Shop Drawings and submittals against the Construction Documents addresses consistency and compatibility between the Construction Manager's detailed documents and the design documents.

The clause sets out the Owner's remedy and notice process where the Construction Manager fails to comply with the Contract to a substantial degree. This allocates responsibility for the consequences of non-compliance and gives the Owner a way to manage it.
The clause requires the Construction Manager to properly provide the Services and comply with the Contract. It sets a 5 Working Day period to correct the default, which enforces performance duties.
Requires the Design-Builder to flag significant deviations between proposed Construction Documents and the Contract Documents, addressing consistency and alignment of design documents.
Contract Documents form the accepted baseline; deviations from it require Owner acceptance and are recorded formally through a Change Order.
Accepted deviations from the Owner's Statement of Requirements are recorded in a Change Order, a formal change mechanism.
The clause expressly addresses toxic or hazardous substances encountered at the Place of the Work and the Contractor's duties to limit exposure and report them.
It allocates responsibility for handling undisclosed hazardous substances not brought by the Contractor, requiring mitigation steps (stopping the Work) and immediate written reporting.
It imposes a duty on how the Work is conducted when hazardous substances are found, including stopping the Work and taking reasonable protective steps.
The clause addresses mould at the Place of the Work, an environmental hazard, including reporting, protective steps and expert investigation.

It assigns responsibility for mitigating harm from mould: the Contractor must take reasonable steps to prevent injury and damage, and the Owner must retain and pay for an independent expert if the parties disagree.
Where the parties disagree on the existence, significance or cause of the mould or the steps to take, the clause sets a process of independent expert determination.
It requires the Contractor to take reasonable steps, including stopping the Work if necessary, which governs how the Work is carried out when mould is found.
The clause obliges the Owner to promptly notify the Construction Manager of any material impact on Project viability, a mitigation and information-sharing duty that helps manage project risk.

The clause governs adjustment of the Contract Time (and entitlement to costs) when the Trade Contractor is delayed by listed events, which is an extension-of-time adjustment under the changes/delays provisions.

It allocates delay risk between the parties: time extension for events beyond the Trade Contractor's control, but no payment for delay costs unless the delay results from the Owner, Consultant or Construction Manager.
It refers to 'unusual delay by common carriers' as a delay cause, which touches delivery of Products, though only as one listed event.
The clause addresses the Contractor's failure to provide or maintain required insurance and gives the Owner the right to procure and maintain it and give evidence of coverage.
It allocates responsibility and a remedy for the Contractor's failure to maintain required insurance, and makes the Contractor bear the cost of the Owner's substitute coverage.
The Owner may deduct the cost of the insurance from amounts due or that may become due to the Contractor, which affects payment mechanics.
Imposes duties on the Construction Manager to communicate Ready-for-Takeover to Trade Contractors and organize completion of the Project, governing how the Work is wrapped up.
Requires establishing, in consultation with Trade Contractors, a reasonable date for finishing the Project, addressing timing of remaining work after Ready-for-Takeover.
The clause governs applications for payment on account, including monthly applications, milestone-based applications, and compliance with Payment Legislation.
It addresses payment of Reimbursable Costs without profit incurred during the Validation Phase, which relates to the cost-reimbursable target cost structure of the IPD contract.

The clause is in the Payment part and states that variance from the Construction Cost Estimate is not grounds for the Owner to withhold fees due to the Construction Manager, which directly governs payment entitlement and withholding.
It allocates the risk of cost estimate variance to the Owner by preventing withholding of the Construction Manager's fees on that basis.

Under the Supervision heading, the clause requires the Design-Builder's appointed representative to represent it at the Place of the Work. It also treats instructions given to that representative as received by the Design-Builder, which sets a duty on how the Work is supervised and directed on site.

The clause states that Specifications, Drawings and models remain the Consultant's property, that signed Contract sets belong to each party, and that their use, copying and alteration are restricted. This addresses ownership rights in Contract Documents.

Allocates responsibility to the Design-Builder for costs, expenses and damages when it knowingly performs work contrary to laws or codes without advising the Owner, which is an explicit risk and responsibility allocation.
Requires the Design-Builder to correct the violations of laws or codes in work performed, which is correction of non-conforming work with its cost consequences.
Sets a duty on how the Work must be performed in compliance with laws, ordinances, rules, regulations and codes, and the consequence of knowingly performing non-compliant work.
The clause governs how the cost of work under a Change Directive is limited to actual costs (starting with labour costs), which determines the resulting adjustment to the Contract Price.

The clause requires the Owner, through the Consultant, to promptly notify the Contractor in writing of observed defects and deficiencies during the warranty period, which is the identification step that leads to correction of defective Work.

It allocates to the Owner a duty to give prompt notice of defects, and it sets the warranty period during which the Contractor is responsible for non-conforming Work, so it manages responsibility for non-conformity.
The clause sets out what an application for payment must include, including supporting documents and evidence for Products delivered but not yet incorporated into the Work.
The clause adjusts the Fee for Construction Services and the Contract Time through the change provisions (GC 6.1, 6.2, 6.3) when the Construction Manager makes good damage it is not responsible for.

It allocates responsibility for damage to the Work or Owner's property not caused by the Construction Manager. The Construction Manager must make good the damage, and the Owner bears the resulting cost and time through adjustment.
It imposes a duty on the Construction Manager to make good damage to the Work, which is a performance obligation in executing the Work.

The clause sets out the Owner's rights to retain and use copies of the plans, Drawings and Specifications. It limits reuse without a written license from the Consultant, which addresses ownership and use rights in the Contract Documents.
The clause ties the Consultant's review and return of Shop Drawings to an agreed schedule, addressing the timing in which portions of the Work proceed.
Consultant review of Shop Drawings addresses the interface between the Contractor's detailed drawings and the design and Contract Documents.
Shop Drawing review is a verification step confirming compliance with the Contract Documents before fabrication and incorporation of Products into the Work.
The clause sits in the claims-for-change-in-Contract-Price process and sets the timing for the Consultant's findings on a claim, which is part of the mechanism for adjusting Contract Price.

The Consultant's findings on a claim by either party, delivered by Notice in Writing within a set time, form a step in the process for resolving matters in question, and precede any further dispute steps.
The clause adjusts the Contract Time and provides cost reimbursement when the Owner causes delay, which is a resulting adjustment to Contract Time and price under the Contract's change provisions.
It allocates the risk and consequences of Owner-caused delay to the Owner through a time extension and reimbursement of the Design-Builder's reasonable costs.

Surety bonds are a contract security mechanism that transfers and mitigates the risk of non-performance; the clause sets requirements for the surety's licensing, for keeping the bonds in good standing until the Contract is fulfilled, and for the bond form.
Sets the Payment Certifier's duty and 20-day timeline to certify or reject the application for Substantial Performance, which triggers holdback release under the payment provisions.
The Payment Certifier must review the Work to verify the validity of the Substantial Performance application, which is a review of the Work by an authorized party.
The clause allocates risk between Owner and Construction Manager by waiving post-Ready-for-Takeover claims, with specified exceptions such as third-party indemnity and warranty claims.
It expressly preserves claims respecting toxic or hazardous substances for which indemnity could be asserted against the Construction Manager.

The clause makes the Contractor and Other IPD Parties responsible for the means, methods, techniques, sequences and safety procedures of the Work, which is a duty governing how the Work is performed and supervised.
The clause assigns responsibility for means, methods and safety procedures to the performing parties, which allocates responsibility for the manner of performance to them.
The clause sets conditions under which a defaulting party is deemed to have cured a default, which allocates and manages the consequences of default and limits termination or suspension rights.

Default triggers concern the Owner's failure to show financing, the Consultant's failure to issue a payment certificate, and non-payment of certified amounts or amounts awarded by adjudication, arbitration or court.
The clause assigns consequences for Owner default and sets the conditions under which the Construction Manager may give default notice, which allocates contractual risk between the parties.
It sets a formal Notice in Writing process for default, which escalates matters in question and refers to amounts awarded by adjudication, arbitration or court.

The clause treats a lien claim as a notice of claim under the waiver-of-claims provisions, so it links to the claims process that governs adjustments to the Contract. It does not create a change mechanism, so the connection is weak.
The clause governs the Trade Contractor's duty to act on a Change Directive, a formal change mechanism, by proceeding promptly with the change in the Work.
It imposes a duty on how the Work is performed, requiring the Trade Contractor to proceed promptly with the directed change.
The clause requires the Trade Contractor to correct or pay for damage caused by warranty corrections under 12.3.4, addressing the consequences of correcting defective or non-conforming Work.
It allocates responsibility to the Trade Contractor for damage arising from warranty corrections, assigning the risk and cost of that consequential damage.
Sets interest on late payments due under the Contract, including compounding and prime rate basis. This is a payment timing and payment-mechanics provision.

Paragraph 6.2.2 applies interest to settled amounts of claims in dispute resolved under Part 7 Dispute Resolution, and to awards by adjudication, arbitration or court. This links payment consequences to the dispute-resolution outcomes.

The clause makes the Owner's failure to furnish financial evidence, the Consultant's failure to issue a payment certificate, and non-payment of certified amounts grounds for default notice. These are payment certification and payment timing matters.
It sets out the conditions under which the Contractor may declare the Owner in default. This allocates and manages contractual risk of Owner non-performance, including financing assurance.
It sets a formal Notice in Writing default process and refers to amounts awarded by arbitration or court. This is an escalation mechanism for unresolved matters between the parties.

The clause states that Specifications, Drawings and models furnished by the Consultant remain the Consultant's property, except signed Contract sets which belong to each party, and restricts their use and copying. This addresses ownership of Contract Documents.
The clause deals with the Contractor's failure to provide or maintain required insurance and gives the Owner the right to procure and maintain it and give evidence of coverage.
It allocates the consequence of the Contractor's failure to maintain insurance by letting the Owner step in and shifting the cost to the Contractor, which mitigates risk.
The clause requires continuity of the Consultant who provides the Design Services, with the replacement holding the former Consultant's status, so design responsibility is preserved.
The clause imposes a duty on the Design-Builder to appoint a replacement Consultant immediately, which governs how the design and construction services are organized and supervised.

The clause requires the Contractor's appointed representative to be at the Place of the Work and deems instructions given to that representative to be received by the Contractor. This sets a supervision and organization duty for how the Work is performed.
The clause caps each party's liability under any legal theory and excludes indirect and consequential damages, which allocates and limits contractual risk between the parties.

Paragraph .1 ties the liability limit to the amount of insurance required under GC 11.1, and paragraph .2 sets a different limit for losses where insurance is not required. Insurance coverage therefore determines the cap.

The clause sets the first step of the dispute-resolution process, requiring the parties to make all reasonable efforts to resolve a dispute by amicable negotiation and to disclose relevant facts, information and documents.
The clause continues the Trade Contractor's obligations for quality, correction and warranty of work performed before termination, which covers correction of defective or non-conforming work.
It keeps responsibility for conformity, quality and warranty with the Trade Contractor after termination, so the risk of non-conforming work stays allocated to it.

Addresses errors, omissions and inconsistencies in the Contract Documents, assigning responsibility for them away from the Construction Manager and requiring reporting to the Consultant for correction, which concerns document consistency.

Allocates the risk of document errors and omissions to the Owner/Consultant side by stating the Construction Manager is not responsible, and sets a mitigation step of reporting and stopping affected work.
Imposes a duty on how the Work proceeds: the Construction Manager must not proceed with affected work until corrected information is received.

The clause addresses payment timing and amounts, allowing portions of the Profit Pool to be paid at milestones determined by the PMT and recorded in Schedule D, under the GC 5.2 Milestone Payments heading.
The Profit Pool is part of the target-cost/fee compensation structure of the IPD contract, and the clause administers how it is distributed at milestones.
The Consultant may order portions of the Work to be examined, which establishes an inspection and examination right.
Work found not in accordance with the Contract Documents is deemed defective and must be corrected under GC 2.4.
The examination verifies compliance of the Work with the Contract Documents, which is a quality assurance function. It is not specific to fabricated Products before incorporation.

The clause requires the Owner, through the Construction Manager, to issue a Change Order or Change Directive where the discovery of artifacts or fossils increases or decreases the Trade Contractor's cost or time, which is a formal change mechanism adjusting price and time.
It allocates responsibility for the cost and time impact of unforeseen artifact and fossil discoveries to the Owner through an adjustment process, so the Trade Contractor is not left with that risk.
The clause imposes a duty on the Owner and Contractor to comply with site health and safety programs, which governs how the Work is carried out at the Place of the Work.

The clause sets out the consequences of the Owner's uncorrected default, allowing the Trade Contractor to suspend the Work or terminate the Contract while preserving other remedies. This allocates default risk and remedies between the parties.
The clause requires a Notice in Writing giving a 5 Working Day cure period before suspension or termination. This is a formal notice and escalation step for a default matter between the parties.
The clause limits the Consultant's Shop Drawing review to conformity with the design concept and general arrangement, addressing the interface between Shop Drawings and the design/Contract Documents.
Consultant review of Shop Drawings is a verification step for compliance before fabrication and incorporation into the Work, and the clause defines the limited scope of that review.
By restricting the review to conformity to design concept and general arrangement only, the clause implicitly leaves responsibility for detailed conformity with the Trade Contractor.
Imposes a duty on the Contractor on how to conduct the Work at the Place of the Work: taking reasonable precautions to protect discovered artifacts and notifying the Consultant upon discovery.
Requires the Contractor to take precautions to prevent removal or damage to discoveries and to give notice, which assigns responsibility for mitigating the risk of loss of such items.
Allocates the risk of a court or public authority order suspending the Work by giving the Contractor a termination right, provided the order was not caused by the Contractor's fault.
The Consultant may reject work that does not conform to the Contract Documents, which is the identification and rejection of non-conforming Work.
The Consultant may require inspection or testing of work whether fabricated, installed or completed, which establishes an inspection and testing authority.
The authority to require testing of work that is fabricated, before or after installation, verifies compliance with the Contract Documents.

The final sentence provides that the Consultant's exercise or non-exercise of authority creates no duty or responsibility to the Contractor, Subcontractors or Suppliers, which allocates responsibility away from the Consultant.

The clause governs the authority and duties of the Payment Certifier, who issues certificates for payment, and requires written consent of both parties to modify them, so it bears on payment certification.
The clause concerns toxic or hazardous substances at the Place of the Work and the investigation of their existence and significance, which is an expressly environmental matter.
It sets a procedure for when the Owner and Contractor disagree: an independent qualified expert investigates and reports to both parties, which is a formal process for resolving a matter in question.
The expert determines whether the Contractor brought the substances onto the site, which establishes responsibility for hazardous substance risk. The Owner also bears the cost of the investigation.

The clause defines the Consultant's authority to act for the Owner in administering the Contract, which sets a limit on how the Work is supervised and administered under the Contract Documents. The link is indirect, so confidence is low.

The Consultant conducts reviews of the Work to verify that Ready for Acceptance With Reservation has been attained and that the application for Ready for Acceptance Without Reservation is valid, which is an on-site inspection/review function by an authorized party.
The clause expressly addresses toxic and hazardous substances legislation and designates the Owner as having control and management of the Place of the Work for existing conditions.
By deeming the Owner to have control and management with respect to existing conditions, the clause allocates responsibility for hazardous substance risk under applicable legislation to the Owner.

The clause sets out exceptions to the limitation of liability (third-party claims, wilful misconduct, fraud, abandonment, violations of law). This allocates residual liability risk to the party at fault.
The clause expressly names violations of applicable environmental legislation as a ground for removing the liability cap, so an environmental obligation is expressly involved.

The clause sets the intended scope of the Contractor's performance, requiring labour, Products and services necessary to perform the Work in accordance with the Contract Documents, while limiting it to what is consistent with or inferable from them.

The clause addresses how the Contract Documents are to be read as a whole, with the Work covered by them or properly inferable from them. This bears on consistency between the documents and the performance of the Work.

The clause governs who may perform portions of the Work by letting the Owner object to a proposed Subcontractor or Supplier and require another bidder, which is an organizational requirement on how the Work is carried out.
The Owner's right to object for reasonable cause before contract signing lets it mitigate risk from unsuitable Subcontractors or Suppliers, a weak but identifiable risk-management effect.
The clause expressly addresses toxic and hazardous substances at the Place of the Project and requires exposure levels to stay within legislated limits.
It assigns to the Owner responsibility for taking reasonable steps to prevent exposure and property damage from pre-existing hazardous substances, which is an allocation of risk.
The clause governs how the Contractor's Fee is adjusted when the Work changes, which is a resulting adjustment to price under the change provisions.
The Contractor's Fee is part of the cost-plus/fee structure, and the clause administers adjustment of that fee through the agreed method, which is a fee-structure mechanism.
The clause requires that changes in the Work arising from integration with Other Contractors or Owner's forces be authorized and valued through Change Orders and Change Directives under GC 6.1-6.3.

The change is triggered by co-ordination and integration of others' work with the Work, which addresses the interface between the Work and other parties' work, though it is not specifically about design documents.

The clause allocates risk between Owner and Contractor by releasing the Owner's known claims after a set date. It carves out exceptions for third-party indemnification, substantial defects, warranty claims and post-Substantial Performance acts.
Exception .4 preserves Owner claims for damages from substantial defects or deficiencies in the Work, and exception .5 preserves warranty claims. Both bear on the consequences of defective Work.
The clause gives the Owner, through the Consultant, the right to change the Work (additions, deletions, revisions) by Change Order or Change Directive and to change the Contract Time by Change Order.

The clause sets out the Owner's remedy where the Construction Manager neglects to properly provide the Pre-construction Services or perform the Work, or otherwise fails to comply with the Contract to a substantial degree. It therefore addresses proper performance of the Work under the Contract Documents.

It allocates the consequences of the Construction Manager's default by giving the Owner a notice-and-correction remedy without prejudice to other remedies. It also requires the Consultant's written statement to support the Owner's action.

The Owner may instruct the Construction Manager to correct the default within 5 Working Days, which concerns identifying and correcting non-conforming performance. The clause does not refer specifically to defective Work, so the link is weaker.

Requires Subcontractors and Suppliers to promptly correct, at their own expense, defects or deficiencies appearing during warranty periods, and to correct or pay for damage resulting from those corrections.
Allocates responsibility and cost for correcting non-conforming work and resulting damage to Subcontractors and Suppliers, with the Contractor obliged to enforce these flow-down obligations.
The clause gives the Contractor control of the Work and the duty to direct and supervise it, which is a core duty governing how the Work is performed and supervised.
By making the Contractor responsible for ensuring the Work conforms to the Contract Documents, the clause allocates responsibility for conformity to the Contractor.

The clause deals with the consequences of removing or replacing non-conforming or defective Work, requiring the Design-Builder to make good other contractors' work damaged by those removals or replacements.

It assigns to the Design-Builder, at its own expense, responsibility for damage to other contractors' work caused by correcting non-conforming Work, which allocates the risk and cost of that correction.

The clause allocates responsibility for damage to the Work and to Owner and adjacent property to the Design-Builder, and carves out exceptions for damage caused by errors in the Owner's Statement of Requirements or by the Owner's acts or omissions.
It imposes a duty on the Design-Builder to protect the Work and property in the course of its operations, which governs how the Work is performed.

The clause allocates the consequences of inaction by providing that failure to act is not a waiver of rights or acquiescence in a breach unless agreed in writing, which protects the parties' contractual positions and allocates risk.

During the Validation Phase, before the Construction Phase, the PMT (a joint team) examines the site and documents information needed for the Design Services and the Work, which is early team participation in developing the design basis.
The clause requires the PMT to examine the site and to perform investigations and surveys, which are on-site inspection and verification activities.
Documenting site information and verifying existing conditions and documentation so they are compatible with the Design Services and the Work ties design inputs to performance of the Work.
Verifying existing conditions, utilities and the accuracy of Owner-provided surveys during Validation identifies and mitigates site-condition risk before the design and cost baseline is set.
The clause governs stoppage of the Work at the Owner's request or through no fault of the Contractor, and deems it a suspension after set periods. This affects how and whether the Work proceeds.

It allocates consequences of stoppage not caused by the Contractor by deeming an Owner suspension after 20 consecutive or 40 cumulative Working Days. This protects the Contractor's position and assigns responsibility to the Owner.
The clause governs release of holdback in Quebec upon Payment Certifier certification, sets a 30-day payment timing, and allows retention for hypothecs, all core payment and holdback mechanics.
The Owner may retain holdback sums to satisfy legal hypothecs or third-party claims enforceable against the Owner, which allocates and mitigates the Owner's financial risk.
The clause governs adjustment of the Contract Time resulting from a Change Directive, including how the adjustment is determined when the parties disagree.
It refers unresolved disagreement over the time adjustment or its method to PART 8 – DISPUTE RESOLUTION, triggering the formal dispute process.

The clause routes disputes on matters outside the Consultant's authority into the negotiation, mediation and arbitration procedures of GC 8.3 and the retention of rights in GC 8.4, which establishes a formal dispute-resolution process.
The clause concerns the Construction Manager's insurance requirements under CCDC 41 and how a reduction in those requirements is addressed before policy renewal.
Any agreed reduction in insurance requirements is recorded in a Change Order, which adjusts the Contract through the formal change mechanism.

The clause fixes the Contract Documents listed in Article C-2 as the sole contractual baseline by superseding all prior negotiations, representations and agreements not listed. This is an entire-agreement provision, so the link to accepted-baseline lock-in is indirect.
The clause provides that if a party does not accept the expert's finding, the disagreement is settled through the Contract's dispute resolution provisions, which triggers a formal dispute process.
The clause sits under GC 9.5 Mould and concerns disagreement over an expert's finding on mould, an environmental condition at the Place of the Work.
The clause requires any Contract Price and Contract Time adjustment arising from delays to be made through the Change Order and Change Directive mechanisms in GC 6.1-6.3.

The clause states the Consultant has no control, charge or supervision of construction means, methods, techniques, sequences or procedures, and that the Construction Manager is responsible for performing the Work in accordance with the Contract Documents.

It allocates responsibility by excluding Consultant liability for the Construction Manager's failure to perform the Work per the Contract Documents and for acts or omissions of Subcontractors, Suppliers and others, leaving that responsibility with the Construction Manager.
The clause addresses mould, an environmental hazard, requiring safe remediation or disposal at the Contractor's expense.
It allocates responsibility and cost to the Contractor for mould caused by its operations, including reimbursement and indemnification of the Owner.
It requires making good damage to the Work and property caused by the Contractor's operations, which is a form of correction with cost consequences.
The clause governs adjustment of the Contract Time (and the limits on cost recovery) when the Design-Builder is delayed by listed events, which is a resulting adjustment to Contract Time and price.
It allocates the risk of delay events between the parties: time is extended for excusable causes, but the Design-Builder bears delay costs unless the delay results from Owner actions.
It lists 'unusual delay by common carriers' as a delay event that extends the Contract Time, which links schedule impact to delivery of Products.
The clause governs how Work performed under a Change Directive is valued and treated pending final determination of the adjustment to the Contract Price.
It states that the undisputed value of Change Directive Work may be included in progress payments, addressing payment timing and eligibility.
The clause sets up the dispute-resolution process by requiring the parties to appoint a Project Mediator under CCDC 40 mediation rules, with fixed time limits and a Notice in Writing trigger.

The clause requires the Contractor to promptly correct defects or deficiencies in the Work at its own expense during the warranty period, which is direct correction of defective Work with cost consequences.
It allocates responsibility and cost for non-conforming Work to the Contractor, an identifiable assignment of risk for defects.
Directs concealed or unknown conditions involving toxic and hazardous substances, artifacts and fossils, or mould to the specific environmental provisions (GC 9.2, 9.3, 9.5).
Allocates responsibility for certain concealed conditions by routing them to separate risk-governing provisions rather than the general concealed-conditions change process.

The clause sets out how a claim for a change in Contract Price is documented through interim and final accounts where the triggering event has a continuing effect. This is part of the claims mechanism for adjusting the Contract Price.

The clause sets out the Owner's duty to make progress payments as certified by the Consultant, release the holdback on Substantial Performance, and pay the final balance, all subject to Payment Legislation and holdback legislation.
The clause governs how payments are made to the Design-Builder when insurance proceeds become due after loss or damage, so it addresses payment mechanics under the Contract.
It refers to payments under property and boiler and machinery insurance policies and directs that they be handled under GC 11.1 – INSURANCE, so it addresses insurance coverage and proceeds.
Under Part 6, the clause adjusts the Contract Time for excusable delays and provides that the Contractor's Fee, GMP and Target Contract Price are adjusted as a result.

It allocates the risk of delay events (strikes, weather, Subcontractor default, causes beyond the Contractor's control) by granting time extensions, while excluding delays caused by the Contractor's own default.
It expressly requires the Contractor's Fee, the GMP and the Target Contract Price to be adjusted as a result of the delay, which is an administration of the GMP/Target Cost mechanism.
The 'unusual delay by common carriers' item links schedule extension to delays in the transport and delivery of Products, but this is only one of several delay causes.

The clause requires that changes in the Work arising from coordination with Other Trade Contractors or the Owner's or Construction Manager's own forces be authorized and valued through the Change Order and Change Directive provisions (GC 6.1-6.3).
The clause sits within execution of the Work and addresses how the Work is integrated with work by others, but it creates no broader performance duty beyond routing changes to the change provisions.
The clause obliges the Trade Contractor to perform the Work required by the Contract Documents, establishing the basic duty governing how the Work is executed.

The clause sets a procedural duty on the Contractor to apply for Ready for Acceptance Without Reservation upon completion, which governs how the Work is brought to completion under the Contract Documents.

States the intent of the Contract Documents to include the labour, Products and services necessary for performing the Work in accordance with them, which sets a broad performance obligation and its scope.

Ties the Trade Contractor's scope to what is consistent with, covered by, or properly inferable from the Contract Documents, which addresses how the documents relate to the Work. It is a weak interpretive-scope link to design and document consistency.
The clause adjusts the Contract Time and provides cost reimbursement for a delay caused by a stop work order, which is a contractual adjustment to time and price under the Part 6 change provisions.
It allocates the risk of a stop work order not caused by the Trade Contractor to the Owner through a time extension and reimbursement of reasonable costs.

Under the Payment part, the clause requires the Owner to give reasonable evidence of financial arrangements to fulfill its obligations, which supports the Owner's payment obligations and payment assurance.

The clause routes disputes on which the Consultant has no authority to make a finding into the negotiation, mediation and arbitration procedures of GC 8.2 and the retention of rights in GC 8.3, so it triggers a formal dispute-resolution process.
The clause requires a joint schedule setting out when allowance items must be ordered so the Work progresses without delay, addressing the timing and order of activities.
The ordering schedule is intended to avoid delaying progress of the Work due to procurement of allowance items (Products), linking schedule impact to procurement.
The clause provides that if a party does not accept the expert's findings, the disagreement is to be settled through the contract's dispute resolution procedure, which establishes a dispute process.
It arises under the Toxic and Hazardous Substances provisions and concerns disagreement over an expert's findings on hazardous substances, which is an environmental issue.
The clause requires the Contractor to furnish the Consultant with certificates and inspection reports relating to the Work, which is part of the inspection procedure and reporting under the Contract.
Furnishing certificates and inspection reports provides verification evidence that Work or Products comply with the Contract Documents, a quality assurance function.

The Consultant receives and reviews written warranties and related documents from the Contractor before forwarding them to the Owner. This is a limited document-verification step, and it is not tied to Products before incorporation into the Work.

The clause gives the Owner, through the Consultant, the right to make additions, deletions or revisions to the Work by Change Order or Change Directive, and to change the Contract Time by Change Order.

The clause requires the Construction Manager to provide, maintain and pay for general liability, automobile, aircraft/watercraft, broad form property, boiler and machinery, equipment and pollution liability insurance, and sets the coverage periods and insureds.

The clause allocates risk of loss or damage and liability between the parties through required coverage, adjustment of losses by the Construction Manager, and the Owner's responsibility for restoration of damage arising from the Owner's own forces or Other Contractors.
Sub-clause .8 requires Contractors' Pollution Liability Insurance, which expressly addresses pollution risk.
Sub-clause .6 ties payment of restoration amounts to the Owner and Construction Manager to the progress payment provisions.
Sub-clause .6(1) entitles the Construction Manager to an extension of Contract Time after loss or damage, and .6(2)-(3) adjust payment for restoration, which is a Contract Time and Price adjustment.

Requires the Owner to pay the Cost of the Work and earned Fee up to termination upon the Consultant's certificate and in accordance with Part 5 – PAYMENT, and to pay compensation for retained Construction Equipment.

Entitles the Owner to take possession of the Work and finish it by whatever method it considers expedient, but without undue delay or expense, which governs how the Work is completed after termination.

Allocates responsibility for obligations, commitments and unliquidated claims between the parties on termination, and excludes amounts payable by the Construction Manager because of neglect or default.

The clause states that the Contract Price amounts are subject to adjustments as provided in the Contract Documents, which points to the contractual mechanisms (Change Orders, Change Directives) for adjusting price, although these are not named.

The clause sets out what happens when the 10 Working Day period for the arbitration notice expires. It allows the parties to refer the unresolved dispute to the courts or to another agreed dispute-resolution process, including arbitration, so it forms part of the formal dispute-resolution procedure.
The clause requires the Design-Builder to furnish the Owner, on request, with inspection reports and test reports, which gives the Owner access to inspection and testing results for the Work.
Requiring copies of certificates and test reports lets the Owner verify that the Work and Products comply with the Contract Documents, which is a quality assurance function.

The clause sets out how claims with a continuing effect are documented, through interim accounts at reasonable intervals and a final account. These are claims procedures, and they may lead to adjustments in Contract Price or Contract Time.

The clause keeps responsibility for Shop Drawing errors and omissions, and for meeting Construction Documents requirements, with the Construction Manager despite the Consultant's review. This allocates responsibility for conformity.
The clause concerns the relationship between Shop Drawings and the Construction Documents, and requires them to meet all Construction Documents requirements despite review.

The clause addresses the effect of the Consultant's review of Shop Drawings, a verification step before fabrication or incorporation into the Work, and says it does not shift compliance responsibility.
Gives the Consultant authority to require inspection or testing of work whether or not fabricated, installed or completed.
Gives the Consultant authority to reject work that does not conform to the Contract Documents, which is the identification and rejection of non-conforming Work.
States that the Consultant's authority to act or not act creates no duty or responsibility to the Construction Manager, Subcontractors or Suppliers, which allocates responsibility for conformity.
Allows the Consultant to require testing of work that is fabricated, to verify compliance with the Contract Documents.

The clause governs how indemnity claims are handled, requiring timely notice and giving the indemnifying party the right to appeal once it assumes liability. This manages the allocation of liability between the parties.

The clause routes disputes and matters in question between the Contractor and Other Contractors to Part 8 Dispute Resolution and deems the Contractor to consent to arbitration where the Other Contractor's contract has a similar agreement to arbitrate.

The clause requires the Owner, through the Consultant, to promptly notify the Construction Manager in writing of observed defects and deficiencies during the warranty period, which is the identification step that triggers correction of defective Work.

The notice concerns defects the Owner or Consultant has observed in the completed Work, which implies a review or observation function. It sets no inspection procedure or access right, so the link is weak.
The clause requires that the Work be governed by the laws of the Place of the Project, which sets a general requirement on how the Work is performed under the Contract.
The clause makes the Construction Manager responsible for the proper performance of the Work, which is a general duty governing how the Work is executed.

It allocates responsibility for performance to the Construction Manager, limited to what the design and Contract Documents permit. Responsibility for design-related limitations therefore stays outside the Construction Manager's scope.

The clause ties the Construction Manager's responsibility to whether the design and Contract Documents permit proper performance, which addresses the compatibility of the design with performing the Work.
The clause limits a party's indemnity obligation to available insurance proceeds for insurable claims, which allocates and caps contractual liability risk between the parties.
It ties the indemnity obligation to insurance policies specified in the Contract Documents and to the proceeds available under them, expressly addressing insurance coverage.

The clause makes the Contractor responsible for establishing, maintaining and supervising health and safety programs in connection with performing the Work, which is a broad duty governing how the Work is organized and supervised.

The clause assigns to the Contractor responsibility for health and safety and the statutory Prime Contractor/Constructor duties, which allocates a category of legal responsibility and risk to the Contractor.
The clause addresses mould presence, requiring the Design-Builder to safely remediate or dispose of mould, which is an environmental/hazardous condition obligation.
It allocates responsibility and cost to the Design-Builder where mould was caused by its operations, including reimbursement of Owner costs and indemnification.
It requires the Design-Builder to make good damage to the Work and property resulting from its operations, which is a corrective obligation, though not strictly non-conforming Work.
The clause is triggered by agreement or an expert's determination under 9.5.2 on causation, which functions as a matter-in-question resolution mechanism.

The clause governs how Change Directives are structured for valuing changes, requiring that unrelated changes not be grouped in one Change Directive, which is part of the formal change mechanism and price adjustment.
The clause addresses mould at the Place of the Project, an environmental hazard, and sets reporting and protective steps.

It assigns responsibility for mitigating harm: the Trade Contractor must take reasonable steps to prevent injury and property damage, including stopping the Work, and the Owner must pay for an independent expert.
Sub-clause .3 sets a process for when the parties disagree on the existence, significance or cause of the mould. An independent expert investigates and determines these matters.
It requires the Trade Contractor to stop the Work if necessary and take protective steps, which governs how the Work is carried out when mould is suspected.
Under the Changes in the Work part, this clause starts the process for concealed or unknown conditions by requiring Notice in Writing, which leads to adjustments in Contract Price and Contract Time.
It allocates the risk of latent or materially differing site conditions by imposing a notice duty on the discovering party before the conditions are disturbed, and within 5 Working Days.

Requires the Contractor to promptly furnish the Consultant with copies of certificates and inspection reports, which supports the inspection process under the heading Review and Inspection of the Work.
Delivery of certificates and inspection reports is a compliance-verification function that documents conformity of Work and Products to the Contract Documents.
Establishes the Trade Contractor's duty over design, erection, operation, maintenance and removal of Temporary Work, which governs how the Work is performed and organized.
Assigns 'sole responsibility' for Temporary Work to the Trade Contractor, which allocates responsibility and risk for those items unless otherwise specified.

Requires the Consultant to make changes to the Contract Documents through the change mechanisms of GC 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 (Change Order and Change Directive) when a variance with laws or a change in codes arises.
Allocates responsibility for legal compliance of the Contract Documents by relieving the Contractor of verification and requiring notice of variances, which manages regulatory risk.
Addresses consistency between the Contract Documents and applicable laws and codes, with the Consultant responsible for revising the documents to resolve variances.
Once Contract Documents are set at bid closing, modifications caused by later code changes must follow the formal change provisions in GC 6.1-6.3.

The clause governs handling of the lien holdback amount, requiring the Owner to deposit it in a joint bank account before the holdback period expires, which is a holdback and payment-timing mechanic tied to lien legislation.

The clause requires the Consultant's interpretations and findings, which are the first step in resolving matters in question, to be issued in writing within a reasonable time. This supports the dispute process, but it does not set out a formal dispute mechanism itself.

The clause addresses the timing and order in which portions of the Work proceed by permitting Owner occupancy of part or all of the Work before Ready-for-Takeover, which implies phased or concurrent use and completion.
The clause requires a joint schedule showing when cash allowance items must be ordered so Work progress is not delayed, which addresses the timing and order in which portions of the Work proceed.
The ordering schedule is intended to avoid delaying the progress of the Work through late procurement of allowance items (Products), linking schedule impact to procurement.
The Construction Manager and Consultant must jointly prepare the schedule, which requires coordination between construction and design roles.
The Trade Contractor assumes responsibility for royalties and patent licence fees and must hold the Owner harmless from patent infringement claims, which allocates and transfers contractual risk.

The clause sets the basis for payment applications: the amount claimed is the proportionate value of Work performed and Products delivered to the Place of the Work as of the last day of the payment period.

The clause sets an order of priority and interpretation rules (scale, dimensions, dates, notes vs. graphics) to resolve conflicts among Drawings, Specifications and other Contract Documents, which addresses consistency and alignment between design documents.
Para .2 requires the Owner to pay the terminated party the Reimbursable Costs properly incurred to the date of termination, subject to set-off or deduction, which addresses payment on termination.

Para .1 lets the remaining parties take possession of the terminated party's Instruments of Service, materials, equipment, products and completed Work. This concerns rights over the Work, products and documents, though it speaks of possession rather than title.
The clause allocates the consequences of a party's default. The remaining parties may set off or deduct losses and damages caused by the default, within the exceptions in GC 10.1.1.
The remaining parties may finish the Project by whatever method the SMT considers expedient, without undue delay or expense. This sets how the Work is completed after termination.
The clause addresses toxic or hazardous substances brought onto the Place of the Work, requiring safe removal and disposal in accordance with applicable legislation.
It allocates responsibility and cost to the Contractor for hazardous substances it brought to the site, including making good damage, reimbursing the Owner and indemnifying the Owner.
The clause concerns tests and inspections performed by others as designated in the Contract Documents, and sets who pays for the samples those tests and inspections require.
It assigns the cost of samples for designated tests and inspections to the Construction Manager, which is an allocation of cost responsibility.

The clause deems fossils, coins, articles of value or antiquity and other remains discovered at the Place of the Work to be the absolute property of the Owner as between Owner and Contractor, which directly addresses ownership and title.

Requires the Contractor to review Shop Drawings and evidence that review by stamp, date and signature before submission to the Consultant, a quality-assurance verification of compliance prior to fabrication and incorporation into the Work.
Shop Drawings interface with the Drawings and Specifications; the Contractor's documented review supports consistency and coordination of design documents with the performance of the Work.
Sets a Contractor duty on how Shop Drawing review is performed and documented during execution of the Work.
The Contractor bears royalty and patent licence fees and must hold the Owner harmless from patent infringement claims, which allocates and transfers risk to the Contractor.

The clause limits and allocates the Design-Builder's liability for Design Services claims to errors, omissions or negligence of the Consultant, and caps it at insurance amounts, which is an identifiable allocation of contractual risk.
It ties the limit of liability to the amount of insurance the Design-Builder is obligated to carry under GC 11.1, expressly addressing insurance coverage.
