The clause addresses responsibility for Design Services, specifically liability for errors, omissions or negligent performance by the Consultant or Other Consultant.
The clause requires a jointly prepared schedule fixing when allowance items must be ordered so the Work progresses in proper timing and sequence.
The ordering schedule exists to avoid delaying the progress of the Work through late procurement of cash allowance items (Products).

The clause allocates to the Owner the risk of damages or costs arising from errors, inconsistencies or omissions in the Owner's Statement of Requirements or other Owner-provided information, relieving the Design-Builder of liability.

It addresses responsibility for errors, inconsistencies and omissions in the Owner's Statement of Requirements, which is a design-input document, and so bears on the consistency of the design information underlying the Design Services.

The clause requires the Owner or Trade Contractors to obtain, maintain and pay for specified coverages (automobile, aircraft/watercraft, contractors' equipment, pollution liability) per CCDC 41, with defined durations.
By requiring specified insurance and allocating responsibility to obtain and pay for it, the clause transfers and manages contractual risk.
Requires Contractors' Pollution Liability Insurance, which expressly addresses pollution and contamination risk.

The clause governs how the Construction Manager organizes the Work, stating that the Specifications' organization and the Drawings' arrangement do not control how it divides the work among Subcontractors and Suppliers, which reflects responsibility for organizing the performance of the Work.
The clause names non-payment of the Construction Manager's compensation for Services as an example of Owner default that lets the CM give a default notice, so it touches payment obligations.
It sets out the consequence of Owner non-compliance, giving the CM a right to notify default as the first step toward termination. This allocates contractual default risk to the Owner.

The clause deals with toxic or hazardous substances at the Place of the Work and sets out the Owner's obligations to remediate and reimburse when the substances were not brought by the Design-Builder.

It allocates responsibility for hazardous substance risk to the Owner, who bears the cost of steps taken, the cost of delay and indemnification when the Design-Builder is not responsible for the substances.
It provides for extension of the Contract Time and reimbursement of the Design-Builder's costs, which adjusts Contract Time and cost without a Change Order.

The clause fixes the contractual baseline by superseding all prior negotiations, representations and agreements not listed in Article A-3, so the listed Contract Documents become the operative baseline. This implicitly supports later changes only through formal contract provisions, but the connection is indirect.
The clause governs how agreed adjustments to Contract Price and Contract Time are recorded in a Change Order and take effect immediately.
It requires the value of work performed under a Change Order to be included in applications for progress payment, addressing payment mechanics.

The clause is part of the negotiation, mediation and arbitration procedure. It sets a 10 Working Day notice window after a request for arbitration under 8.3.6 and determines when disputes are referred to arbitration.

The clause allocates the risk of the Trade Contractor's insolvency or bankruptcy to the Owner's benefit by giving the Owner a right to terminate the Trade Contractor's right to continue with the Work, without prejudice to other remedies.
The clause sets a duty on the Design-Builder about the Products used in performing the Work: they must be new and, if unspecified, of a quality consistent with the Contract Documents.
It places responsibility on the Design-Builder for conformity of Products with the Contract Documents, and Owner acceptance of the use of unspecified Products acts as a control on non-conformity.

The clause allocates the risk of Owner insolvency by giving the Contractor a right to terminate the Contract by Notice in Writing without prejudice to other remedies, which is an identifiable risk transfer and mitigation mechanism.

The clause sets the mediation step of the dispute process. After 10 Working Days from the responding party's Notice in Writing, the parties must ask the Project Mediator to help resolve unresolved disputes under CCDC 40 rules.

The clause designates a Payment Certifier who reviews applications for payment and certifies the value of Design Services, Work performed and Products delivered to the Place of the Work, which is payment certification.

The clause requires the Consultant to issue Supplemental Instructions (Specifications, Drawings, etc.) that supplement the Contract Documents as needed for the Work, which addresses the consistency and completeness of design documents relative to performance of the Work.
Instructions are to be furnished promptly or per an agreed schedule between Consultant and Contractor, which links the timing of design information to progress of the Work.
The clause concerns Profit Pool amounts previously paid as milestone payments under GC 5.2 and lets the Owner recover any overpayment on termination, which is a payment-entitlement mechanism.
It allocates the financial consequence of termination by making the Design/Construction Team repay amounts paid beyond its entitlement.

Sets out the Design/Construction Team's duties during the Construction Phase, including performing the Work, procuring subcontractors and suppliers, and completing tasks to reach Ready-for-Takeover, under PMT oversight.

Requires completion of the remainder of the Design Services during the Construction Phase, and delivery of record drawings and digital models, which addresses design responsibility and document alignment with the Work.
Requires final testing, start-up and commissioning of utilities, operational systems and equipment, which are testing procedures on the Work.
The clause imposes a duty on the Contractor governing how the Work is conducted at the site, requiring reasonable precautions to protect discovered artifacts and notification of the Consultant.

The clause governs approval of payment applications by the PMT in the amount applied for or as properly due, within 10 days and subject to Payment Legislation, which is payment certification and timing.

After a party's termination during Validation, the remaining parties must formally revise the contract schedules (costs, profit pool, tasks matrix) and add a replacement party by executed schedule. This is a formal amendment to the contractual baseline, but it does not concern an accepted baseline after Validation.

The clause requires the PMT to organize PITs into cross-functional teams that vary by Project stage, which sets a general organizational and supervisory structure for carrying out the Design Services and the Work.
The clause sets a requirement that all required insurance policies be placed with insurers licensed in the jurisdiction of the Place of the Work, which defines and maintains insurance requirements.
Imposes a broad duty on the Contractor to provide and pay for labour, Products, equipment, utilities and services necessary to perform the Work in accordance with the Contract.
Allocates to the Contractor the responsibility and cost of supplying all resources necessary for the Work, which is an implied allocation of resourcing and cost risk.
